Reni Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Reni, Ukraine

Not demolished. Existing no later than 1830 per epigraphic data, this cemetery remains operational today; a regular caretaker maintained it with full fencing in the mid-1990s, and a small local community now continues its upkeep. Jewish settlement began in the 18th century; 22 families lived there by 1847, with population reaching 730 (11%) by 1897. Zionist organizations were active from the early 20th century; a synagogue and cemetery operated by 1910, when population reached 1,018 (11%), rising slightly to 1,201 by 1930. Wehrmacht occupation from July 19, 1941 saw about 18 Jews murdered that August; the remaining roughly 300 were imprisoned in a camp before October 4, 1941 deportation to Transnistria. Some Jews returned after 1945, and by 2005 Reni again had a Jewish population.
